exposure: Non-SGA neonates identified as normal at ultrasound examination (true negative) vs. non-SGA neonates diagnosed incorrectly as SGA (false positive)
SGA neonates diagnosed correctly at ultrasound examination (true positive) vs. SGA neonates that went undiagnosed (false negative)
screening for small-for-gestational-age (SGA) fetuses by ultrasound biometry at 30-35 weeks' gestation
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of ultrasound for SGA prediction
Obstetric outcomes (planned preterm delivery, elective Cesarean section)
Neonatal health status (5-min Apgar score, cord blood pH at birth, need for neonatal resuscitation)
cohort: Pregnant women recruited from two French university maternity centers between 2003 and 2006
finding: Third-trimester ultrasound screening for SGA had poor performance, missing a large number of SGA neonates and potentially leading to unnecessary interventions without improving neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The study found that routine third-trimester ultrasound screening for small-for-gestational-age (SGA) may lead to an increase in elective cesarean sections in pregnancies where the fetus is incorrectly diagnosed as SGA, without improving neonatal outcomes in pregnancies where SGA is undiagnosed.
